newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-RUSEDSKI USES LUCKY BALLS AND TOWELS TO WIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RUSEDSKI USES LUCKY BALLS AND TOWELS TO WIN.

text.p: Greg Rusedski is a big, strapping 23-year-old with weightlifter's shoulders and a serve like a heat-seeking missile.
On Monday and Tuesday he slammed down 27 aces to hurl seventh seeded Australian Mark Philippoussis, the only man to record a serve faster than his own, out of Wimbledon.
But the Canadian-born Briton, who wowed the partisan Centre Court crowd with his 7-6 7-6 6-3 exhibition of power and ferocity, is a bundle of nervous superstition.
On court he is never without his towel, which he uses like a security blanket, hugging it and wiping his brow between points.
"Every time I take a towel is when I am down and I lost a point. So I want to regroup myself and get ready," the 1.92m tall left-hander said.
"I know it is a little bit awkward or strange to watch, but if it works you don't change it usually," he added.

Rusedski, who grins widely apparently unembarrassed by his compulsive behaviour, is on top grass form after reaching the semifinal of the Queen's tournament earlier this month, bowing out only after a 20-18 tie-break against Goran Ivanisevic. He went on to win the Nottingham competition last Sunday.
But he is still superstitious about the balls.
He used the same ball for his last service game on Tuesday, calling for the ball girls to throw it back to him.
"A lucky ball, I guess. It seemed to work all right. It won me three straight points so it must have been doing all right.''
Earlier in the day he had met a group of sick children and exchanged autographs. He said he would keep their signatures in his bag from now on for luck.
It was not luck that won him the upset over Philippoussis, ranked 13 in the world, but determination.
His served consistently well, with only three double faults to the Australian's 13 and kept his nerve on the big points.
"When a guy serves that big it's hard to do anything," a dejected Philippoussis said afterwards.
"The crowd helped him - he was fired up with adrenaline."
"If Greg can serve like that in his other matches, who knows how far he can go. He's going to have a good tournament, I think."
